\chapter{Chapter05 — Improved FKN}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.ImprovedFKN}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Balanced lift with a designated coordinate]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.permuteInput}
For a Boolean function $f$ on $n$ sign coordinates and an index $i$ among those
coordinates, define a Boolean function on $n+1$ coordinates by first swapping coordinate
$0$ with the coordinate corresponding to $i$, then applying the balanced lift of $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Real-valued balanced lift under permutation]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift_toReal}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift_toReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.permuteInput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$, let $f\colon\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $i$ be one of the $n$
coordinates. The real-valued function associated with the lift obtained by swapping the
new first coordinate with coordinate $i+1$ is the real-valued balanced lift composed
with that coordinate permutation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real lift at a positive leading sign]
\lean{FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_one'}
\label{FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_one'}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.balancedFKNLift_fin_cons_one}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from $\{-1,1\}^n$ to the signs
$\{\pm1\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. After interpreting the outputs as real
numbers, the balanced lift of $f$ at the vector with first coordinate $1$ and remaining
coordinates $x$ equals $f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real lift at a negative leading sign]
\lean{FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_neg_one'}
\label{FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_neg_one'}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.balancedFKNLift_fin_cons_neg_one, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from $\{-1,1\}^n$ to the signs
$\{\pm1\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. After interpreting the outputs as real
numbers, the balanced lift of $f$ at the vector with first coordinate $-1$ and remaining
coordinates $x$ equals $-f(-x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients under input negation]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_negatedInput_toReal'}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_negatedInput_toReal'}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{\pm1\}$,
and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the function
$x\mapsto -f(-x)$ is $-(-1)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Singleton Fourier coefficient under the balanced lift]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_balancedFKNLift_succ'}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_balancedFKNLift_succ'}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_neg_one', FABL.balancedFKNLift_toReal_fin_cons_one', FABL.firstCoordinateSlice, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_negatedInput_toReal', FABL.fourierCoeff_tailFrequency, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Define a function on $\{-1,1\}^{n+1}$ by $F(z)=z_0
f((z_0z_1,\ldots,z_0z_n))$. Then the Fourier coefficient of $F$ at the singleton
coordinate $i+1$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a balanced lift]
\lean{FABL.mean_improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\label{FABL.mean_improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff_comp_permuteInput, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift_toReal, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_balancedFKNLift, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.permuteFinset}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and choose a coordinate
$i$. Form the balanced lift of $f$ to $n+1$ coordinates, after swapping the first
coordinate with coordinate $i+1$. The uniform mean of the resulting sign-valued
function, viewed as real-valued, is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier Weight of the Balanced Lift]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_improvedFKNBalancedLift}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_comp_permuteInput, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_balancedFKNLift, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton, FABL.fourierWeightAtMost, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift_toReal, FABL.permuteFinset}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function and let $i$ be a coordinate. Form a
function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube by first swapping coordinate $0$ with
coordinate $i+1$, then applying the balanced lift, whose value at $z$ is $z_0
f((z_0z_{j+1})_{j=0}^{n-1})$. The resulting level-one Fourier weight equals the Fourier
weight of $f$ on levels zero and one combined.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the balanced lift]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_improvedFKNBalancedLift_zero}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_improvedFKNBalancedLift_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.balancedFKNLift, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_balancedFKNLift_succ', FABL.fourierCoeff_comp_permuteInput, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift_toReal, FABL.permuteFinset}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Form the balanced lift of $f$ to $n+1$ coordinates and then swap
its input coordinates $0$ and $i+1$. The Fourier coefficient of this function at the
singleton frequency $\{0\}$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate slice of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNSlice}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNSlice}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.Sign}
For a Boolean function $g$ on $n+1$ sign coordinates and a sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$, define
its slice at $b$ by fixing the first coordinate to $b$ and evaluating $g$ on the
remaining $n$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Real-valued first-coordinate slice]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNSlice_toReal}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNSlice_toReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.Sign, FABL.firstCoordinateSlice, FABL.improvedFKNSlice}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$, let $g\colon\{\pm1\}^{n+1}\to\{\pm1\}$, and fix a sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$. The
real-valued function associated with the restriction of $g$ to inputs whose first
coordinate is $b$ equals the first-coordinate slice of the real-valued function
associated with $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Nonzero coordinates]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, define the set of free coordinates among $n+1$ coordinates to
consist of every coordinate other than coordinate $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Indexing the nonzero coordinates]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNTailIndexEquiv}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNTailIndexEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
For a natural number $n$, define an equivalence from the $n$ indices to the free
coordinates among $n+1$ coordinates by sending each index to its successor coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fixed index at coordinate zero]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKNHeadFixedIndex}
\label{FABL.improvedFKNHeadFixedIndex}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
For a natural number $n$, define the fixed index associated with the free coordinates
among $n+1$ coordinates to be coordinate $0$, which is not in that set.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign-cube combination with a fixed head]
\lean{FABL.combineSignCube_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\label{FABL.combineSignCube_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_fixed, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_free, FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates, FABL.improvedFKNHeadFixedIndex, FABL.improvedFKNTailIndexEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every sign vector $x$ of length $n$, and every assignment
$z$ of signs to the coordinate $0$ in a sign cube of dimension $n+1$, combine the signs
of $x$ on coordinates $1,\ldots,n$ with $z$ at coordinate $0$. The resulting sign vector
is the vector with first coordinate $z(0)$ and remaining coordinates given by $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a restricted slice]
\lean{FABL.mean_signRestriction_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\label{FABL.mean_signRestriction_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.combineSignCube_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates, FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates, FABL.improvedFKNHeadFixedIndex, FABL.improvedFKNSlice, FABL.improvedFKNTailIndexEquiv, FABL.mean, FABL.signRestriction, FABL.signRestriction_apply, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g$ be a function from the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube to $\{-1,1\}$. Leave all
coordinates except coordinate $0$ free, and fix coordinate $0$ to a sign $b$. The mean,
over the free coordinates, of the restricted function's real-valued sign equals the mean
of the $n$-variable slice of $g$ obtained by fixing its first coordinate to $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Means of the two slices]
\lean{FABL.mean_improvedFKNSlices}
\label{FABL.mean_improvedFKNSlices}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_insert_zero_tailFrequency, FABL.fourierCoeff_tailFrequency, FABL.improvedFKNSlice, FABL.improvedFKNSlice_toReal, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $g:\{−1,1\}^{n+1}\to\{−1,1\}$ have uniform mean
zero. For $b\in\{−1,1\}$, let $g_b$ be the restriction of $g$ to inputs whose first
coordinate is $b$. Then the mean of $g_1$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at the
singleton consisting of the first coordinate, and the mean of $g_{-1}$ is the negative
of that coefficient.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p129-b003}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $g$ be a function from the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^{n+1}$
to $\{\pm1\}$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb R$. For every assignment of signs to the
coordinates other than coordinate $0$, suppose the absolute value of the mean of the
resulting one-coordinate restriction of $g$ is at least $1-\delta$, and suppose $0\le
1-\delta$. Then the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $g$, viewed as a
real-valued function, on the singleton sets $\{1\},\ldots,\{n\}$ is at most
$4\delta^2\log_2(2/\delta)$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, choose a coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and choose whether to negate its dictator. The quantity one minus
twice the fraction of inputs on which $f$ differs from that signed dictator is at most
the absolute value of the singleton Fourier coefficient of $f$ at coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Improved FKN approximation]
\lean{FABL.improvedFKN}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p129-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p129-b006
}
\label{FABL.improvedFKN}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.exercise5_38_sqrt_lower_bound, FABL.exercise5_38a, FABL.exists_signedDictator_relativeHammingDist_eq_abs_fourierCoeff, FABL.fknImprovementEta, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_improvedFKNBalancedLift_zero, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_eq_sum_singleton, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.fourierWeightAtMost, FABL.fourierWeightAtMost_one_eq_empty_add_sum_singleton, FABL.improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.improvedFKNFreeCoordinates, FABL.improvedFKNHeadFixedIndex, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_improvedFKNBalancedLift, FABL.mean_improvedFKNSlices, FABL.mean_signRestriction_improvedFKNFreeCoordinates, FABL.one_sub_two_mul_relativeHammingDist_le_abs_fourierCoeff, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.signRestriction, FABL.signValue, FABL.signedDictator, FABL.sum_sq_tail_fourierCoeff_le_of_restrictions}
\difficulty{6}
Let $C\ge1$ and suppose that for every positive integer $m$, every Boolean function
$g\colon\{\pm1\}^m\to\{\pm1\}$, and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$0\le\varepsilon$ and $1-\varepsilon\ge0$, if the level-one Fourier weight of $g$ is at
least $1-\varepsilon$, then some signed dictator on $m$ coordinates differs from $g$ on
at most a fraction $C\varepsilon$ of inputs. Now let $n$ be a positive integer and let
$f\colon\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ satisfy $0\le\delta$, $1-\delta\ge0$, and level-one
Fourier weight at least $1-\delta$. Then some signed dictator differs from $f$ on at
most a fraction $\delta/4+16C^2\delta^2\max\{\log_2(1/(C\delta)),1\}$ of inputs.
\end{theorem}
